response.body:
## Objective

Use the waiting window before Databento responds to determine the simplest, strongest long-term stack for the project and eliminate work that maintained upstream tools already solve.

This is a broad architecture/adoption audit, not an alpha experiment and not another FMBH/security-master review.

Base/source of truth: `feat/alpaca-paper-foundation` after merged PR #8 (`b5b06af7a876ebb4c7fc9ab6f63cbaed9ef2aafe`).

## End goal

A broker- and data-vendor-agnostic US equity research/trading system that can eventually:
- build point-in-time/survivorship-safe research universes
- ingest SEC filings, earnings/guidance, macro/Fed/government/regulation/tariff/sanction/contract/news/geopolitical events
- compare strong cheap quant/statistical baselines against AI/text/hybrid methods
- measure incremental net alpha after costs/slippage
- automate factor/signal discovery where justified
- backtest reproducibly
- paper trade safely
- later execute through Alpaca, IBKR or another broker without redefining scientific truth
- run long research/development tasks with checkpoint/resume and minimal owner relay.

## Mandatory upstream qualification

Inspect CURRENT maintained code/docs/releases and exact revisions where practical for at least:
- TauricResearch/TradingAgents
- Microsoft RD-Agent / RD-Agent(Q)
- FinRL / FinRL-X
- QuantConnect LEAN
- Microsoft Qlib
- NautilusTrader
- serious maintained event/news/macro research tooling or data connectors that materially overlap the planned stack
- any other clearly stronger maintained framework discovered during review.

Do not rely on marketing summaries or star counts. Inspect implementation boundaries, licenses, maintenance, tests/examples, supported data/execution paths and known limitations.

## Evaluate against the actual project

For each relevant system/component, determine whether it can materially help with:
1. point-in-time/no-lookahead handling
2. survivorship-safe universe construction
3. SEC as-filed/fundamental ingestion
4. macro/Fed/government/regulation/news/event ingestion
5. quant baselines and factor discovery
6. LLM/AI strategy research
7. hybrid strategy research
8. realistic backtesting/costs/slippage
9. portfolio/risk management
10. paper/live execution
11. future IBKR integration
12. broker independence
13. data-provider independence
14. checkpoint/resume and long-running autonomous research
15. experiment provenance/reproducibility
16. ability to measure incremental AI alpha versus cheap controls
17. licensing, operational burden and expected cost.
18. multi-agent orchestration quality: persistent state, parallel agents, handoffs, approvals and unattended continuation.
19. whether the framework demonstrates trading edge or merely automates analysis/coding.

## Required decisions

For each major planned component return exactly one:
- `ADOPT` — use upstream substantially as-is
- `INTEGRATE` — use a bounded upstream component behind our contract
- `BENCHMARK` — use as challenger/reference, not production authority
- `KEEP_OURS` — project-specific logic is necessary
- `REJECT` — wrong fit, unsafe, stale, lock-in, or scientifically unsuitable.

Explicitly identify:
- what we should stop building immediately
- what we should never build ourselves
- what parts of the current repo remain uniquely necessary
- whether TradingAgents, RD-Agent, Qlib, LEAN, FinRL-X or Nautilus can accelerate the path to actual alpha testing
- the cleanest research-to-IBKR path without binding research truth to IBKR
- the cleanest architecture for government/macro/news/event signals
- the simplest credible stack you would choose if starting this project from zero today.

## Efficiency requirement

Do not create implementation code during this audit unless a tiny compatibility probe is necessary to falsify an integration claim.

Prefer deleting/planning-to-delete bespoke generic plumbing over adding another framework.

Do not duplicate the already-completed Databento/security-master review. Treat the historical security-master backbone as an external contract and evaluate only how candidate frameworks consume it.

## Scientific/trading boundaries

- Do not change Amendment 005 or any research registration.
- Do not alter FMBH status.
- Do not advance candidate #2.
- Do not run alpha experiments.
- Do not make paid provider/data/model calls.
- Do not buy or subscribe to anything.
- Do not enable Paper or Live trading.
- Do not expose broker/data credentials.

## Output

Persist one concise architecture/adoption report plus a machine-readable decision table.

Finish with:
- `TARGET_STACK` — the recommended minimal long-term stack
- `STOP_BUILDING_NOW` — generic components to stop building
- `NEXT_3_TASKS` — the three highest-information-value tasks that can proceed after this audit, with dependencies and whether each can run before the Databento answer
- `API_AUTOMATION_VALUE_GATE` — concrete criteria for when paying for unattended API automation becomes worthwhile.

Use HIGH reasoning. This is an architecture/build-vs-adopt audit.
response.title: Build-vs-adopt audit for the long-term AI trading stack
